resolutions.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' is inferred, not literal. Youm7 (21 Jan 2021, Petroleum Ministry project list) lists 'khat Borg El Arab/Midor, 10km, 24-inch, cost 120M EGP, planned completion March 2021'. Hapijournal (10 Jun 2021, PM project-review meeting) reports the same 24in/10km line from Borg El Arab feeding the Midalik/Midor power station at 68% physical progress. No later source found stating completion date explicitly, but both a Jan-2021 near-completion project list and a Jun-2021 68%-progress status (up from presumably lower in Jan) place completion squarely in the StartYear1=2021 window GEM already carries; no contradicting evidence of delay/cancellation found. Recommend a future sweep look for an explicit 2021/2022 commissioning confirmation if available.

Both sources explicitly list this as a natural-gas ('al-ghaz al-tabi'i') line within Egypt's national gas network (al-shabaka al-qawmiyya lil-ghazat al-tabi'iyya), built/operated by GASCO. Two independent outlets, explicit fuel type. High confidence.

'Transmission' is inferred, not stated verbatim. Both sources describe this 24in trunk feeder as part of the national high-pressure gas grid (fed from/through GASCO pressure-reduction & measurement stations, e.g. the Borg El Arab station cited by almalnews at 6M m3/day capacity) delivering bulk gas to the Midor refinery/Midalik industrial expansions -- consistent with GEM's transmission-grade convention for GASCO trunk feeders (vs. local distribution). No source uses the word 'distribution' for this line.

Youm7 (Jan 2021, official Petroleum Ministry project list): 'khat Borg El Arab/Midor... planned completion March 2021' (mukhattat al-intihaa: Maris 2021). Hapijournal (Jun 2021, PM meeting minutes): same line at 68% physical progress as of that date -- consistent trajectory toward a 2021 completion, matching GEM's StartYear1=2021. Two independent contemporaneous sources agree on the year.

Both sources state the length verbatim as '10 km' ('bi-tul 10 km' / '10 km min Borg El Arab'). Youm7: 'khat Borg El Arab/Midor bi-tul 10 km -- qutr 24"'. Hapijournal: 'khat qutr 24" bi-tul 10 km min Borg El Arab li-taghdhiyat mahattat kahraba Midalik/Midor'. Exact match to GEM's LengthKnown=10.00 km from two independent, contemporaneous (2021) government-sourced reports.

Both sources give diameter 24-inch ('qutr 24"') verbatim; a third independent trade outlet, almalnews.com (19 Aug 2021, archived -- live URL now 404), corroborates: 'khat Borg El Arab/Midor qutr 24 bousa li-tawseel al-ghaz al-tabi'i ila tawse'aat sharikatay Midor wa Midalik'. Three independent 2021 sources agree on 24in. High confidence.

Both sources describe the line originating at Borg El Arab. Almalnews specifically names the 'Borg El Arab station' (mahattat Borg El Arab) with 6M m3/day capacity feeding the Midor/Midalik expansions (1.44M m3/day); hapijournal confirms the line runs 'min Borg El Arab' to the Midalik/Midor power station. Live almalnews URL 404s (site restructured) -- cite the Aug-2024 Wayback snapshot, which passes url_verifier and matches the live-crawled title/body used for extraction.

Both sources place the line running from Borg El Arab (a district of Alexandria governorate) to feed the Midor refinery / Midalik expansion, which sits at El-Ameriya (also Alexandria governorate) -- matching GEM's StartLocation=Borg El Arab/Alexandria and EndLocation=Al ameryia/Alexandria, Egypt exactly. No source gives coordinates finer than the town names.

Youm7 gives the project cost verbatim: 'khat Borg El Arab/Midor bi-tul 10 km -- qutr 24" taklifat al-mashru': 120 milyoun jinayh' = 120,000,000 EGP -- exact match to GEM's SegmentCost=120000000.00 EGP. Searched hapijournal, almalnews, dostor, masrawy, elmostqpalelyuom and others for a second cost figure specific to THIS line (as opposed to the larger, separately-costed Al-Ameriya/El-Alamein 32in/120km line at 540M-2bn EGP quoted elsewhere, which is a different pipeline feeding the same Midor/Midalik expansions -- do not conflate). No second source states a cost for the Borg El Arab/Midor line specifically, so this remains single-source/medium tier despite being an exact, unambiguous figure from an authoritative Petroleum-Ministry-sourced project list.

PARTIAL/INFERRED, FLAG FOR REVIEW. All three project reports (youm7, hapijournal, almalnews) name the builder/implementer as GASCO (al-Sharika al-Misriyya lil-Ghazat al-Tabi'iyya), NOT 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) by name. Wikipedia's Egyptian Natural Gas Company page confirms GASCO is a subsidiary of EGAS with EGAS holding a 70% direct equity stake (not 100%) -- so GEM's Owner1='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' at 100% is a reasonable but not literal match: it names the parent state holding company rather than the 70%-owned operating subsidiary (GASCO) that the primary sources credit with building/operating this specific line. This mirrors GEM's established convention elsewhere in the Egypt gas set (attributing GASCO trunk-network assets to the EGAS holding parent), but no source states EGAS itself, nor a 100% stake in this asset. Recommend flagging to Update for a possible Owner1=GASCO (with EGAS as parent/OwnerParent, if that column exists) correction rather than silently accepting; deferring the recommendation per standing rules, not overwriting.
